Erythromycin and Ethinyl Estradiol/Etonogestrel: Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and lactobionate can increase the levels or effects of etonogestrel by inhibiting the CYP3A4 enzyme, while also potentially decreasing the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. These interactions may require alternative drugs or close monitoring. 2. Erythromycin Stearate: This form of erythromycin can decrease the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Close monitoring is advised. 3. Eslcarbazepine Acetate: This drug can decrease the levels or effects of etonogestrel and ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative contraception methods or additional non-hormonal birth control are recommended. 4. Etravirine: This medication reduces the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol and etonogestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, so caution and monitoring are necessary. 5. Exemestane: Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of exemestane due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Exemestane should not be used concurrently with estrogen-containing products. 6. Exenatide: Ethinyl estradiol and etonogestrel may reduce the effects of exenatide by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogens can impair glucose tolerance, so glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. 7. Fedratinib: Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels of fedratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs used. 8. Felbamate: This drug decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance is unclear, but monitoring is advised. 9. Fexinidazole: This drug increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing the risk of adverse effects. Alternative drugs are recommended. 10. Fezolinetant: Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels of fezolinetant by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 11. Finererone: Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels of finererone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring, including serum potassium levels, are recommended. 12. Flibanserin: Ethinyl estradiol increases the risk of adverse effects from flibanserin when co-administered with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Close monitoring is necessary. 13. Fluconazole: This drug increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol and etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 14. Fluvoxamine: Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels of fluvoxamine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 15. Fosamprenavir: This drug increases the levels of etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with ethinyl estradiol may alter hormone levels, and non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 16. Fosphenytoin: This drug decreases the levels of etonogestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. 17. Fostemsavir: This drug increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Dose adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 18. Frovatriptan: Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels of frovatriptan by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear, but monitoring is advised. 19. Grapefruit: Grapefruit increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol and etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 20. Green Tea: Ethinyl estradiol increases green tea levels by decreasing elimination. Monitoring is recommended. 21. Griseofulvin: This drug decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol and etonogestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing contraceptive efficacy. Non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 22. Hydrocortisone: This drug decreases the levels of etonogestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 23. Idelalisib: This drug increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided. 24. Iloperidone: This drug increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 25. Imipramine: Ethinyl estradiol may increase antidepressant serum concentrations by decreasing oxidative metabolism, potentially leading to increased adverse effects. Monitoring is advised. 26. Indinavir: This drug increases the levels of etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 27. Insulin (Various Types): Ethinyl estradiol and etonogestrel may decrease the hypoglycemic effects of insulin by impairing glucose tolerance. Glycemic control should be closely monitored in diabetic patients. 28. Itraconazole: This drug increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol and etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 29. Ketoconazole: This drug increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol and etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 30. Lamotrigine: Ethinyl estradiol decreases lamotrigine levels by inducing glucuronidation, potentially reducing its efficacy. Monitoring is necessary. 31. Lapatinib: This drug increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol and etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 32. Letrozole: Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of letrozole due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration is not recommended. 33. Levofloxacin: This drug decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitoring is advised. 34. Liraglutide: Ethinyl estradiol and etonogestrel may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of liraglutide by impairing glucose tolerance. Glycemic control should be monitored. 35. Lixisenatide: This drug delays gastric emptying, potentially reducing the absorption of ethinyl estradiol. Oral contraceptives should be taken at least 1 hour before or 11 hours after lixisenatide administration. 36. Lomitapide: Ethinyl estradiol increases lomitapide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The lomitapide dose should not exceed 30 mg/day. 37. Lonafarnib: Ethinyl estradiol increases lonafarnib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 38. Metformin: Ethinyl estradiol and etonogestrel may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of metformin. Glycemic control should be monitored. 39. Metronidazole: This drug decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitoring is advised. 40. Metyrapone: Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of metyrapone. Discontinuation of estrogens may be advisable during metyrapone administration. 41. Midazolam: Ethinyl estradiol increases midazolam levels by inhibiting metabolism, potentially increasing benzodiazepine serum concentrations. Monitoring is recommended. 42. Miconazole Vaginal: This drug increases the levels of etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 43. Marijuana: This substance increases the levels of etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 44. Mavacamten: This drug decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol and etonogestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to contraceptive failure. Non-hormonal contraception is recommended. This summary highlights the importance of monitoring and adjusting therapy when these drugs are co-administered with ethinyl estradiol or etonogestrel.
